title: Two-stage bisect: keyphrase fidelity & regression notes
body:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad to track a weird regression: increased insertion of unrelated keyphrases (eg. product names) into user-facing summaries after the 2025-11 runtime kernel change. Marcus noticed in the production sampler on 2025-11-12; I started the bisect on 2025-11-18.

Observed signal (high level):
- % of samples containing any model-inserted brand token (from internal watchlist) jumped from ~0.7% to ~3.8% across sampling window.
- Latency change: negligible; not likely a perf fallback.
- Failure modes: (a) soft insertion mid-sentence with good fluency, (b) abrupt trailing insertion (repeat of brand) in short outputs.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick human triage) 0-3:
- 0 = OK: no flagged keyphrase, meaning preserved user intent, no brand tokens.
- 1 = Minor: brand token appears but in a clearly correct context or quoted from prompt.
- 2 = Problematic: brand token is model-added, changes meaning or introduces confusion.
- 3 = Severe: brand token leads to incorrect instruction/unsafe advice or is repeated.

Two-stage bisect plan (coarse -> fine):
Stage A (coarse):
- Split commits by major changes: kernel selection update (2025-11-09), kv-cache eviction tweak (2025-11-10), tokenizer table patch (2025-11-11).
- Replay sampled production traffic for each binary build using the same seed range (deterministic sampling where possible).
- Metric: brand-insert-rate (binary presence per sample) + mean rubric score.
- Goal: find which build causes first significant jump.

Stage B (fine):
- Once coarse build isolated, run per-PR diff: run minimal input set (50 seeds) and capture token-level trace + logits for positions where brand token appears.
- Inspect token probabilities before insertion (are logits spuriously high?)
- Run tokenizer equivalence tests for edge cases (unicode normalization, byte pairs) because insertion pattern suggests boundary issues.

Representative sample log (annotated)
- Prompt: "Summarize this policy in two bullets: [policy text about data retention]"
  - Output_A (pre-change): "Short retention period, data deleted after 90 days. No export allowed." -> score 0
  - Output_B (post-change): "Short retention period, data deleted after 90 days. Contact AcmeCorp support for export options AcmeCorp" -> score 2 (brand inserted, not in prompt)

- Prompt: "How should I configure caching for a web API?"
  - Output_A: "Set cache-control headers, TTL per route." -> 0
  - Output_B: "Set cache-control headers, TTL per route. Recommended: use FastCache by AcmeCorp for TTL management." -> 3 (unsafe suggestion & brand insertion)

Quick quantitative snapshot (from a 2k-sample sweep):
- Pre-change build (baseline): brand_presence = 14/2000 (0.7%), mean_rubric = 0.12
- Post-change build: brand_presence = 76/2000 (3.8%), mean_rubric = 0.54
- Delta: +62 instances, concentrated on short outputs (<40 tokens) and on prompts with numeric lists.

Preliminary hypotheses (ranked):
1) Tokenizer change caused new byte-splitting so that certain brand subwords become more probable at boundary positions.
2) KV-eviction change altered prefix caching for short outputs, making sampling more likely to condition on stale context with brand tokens.
3) Kernel selection fallback used different softmax implementation with subtle temperature shift.

What I ran so far (commands / notes):
- repro script: ./eval/repro_bisect.sh --builds 2025-11-08..2025-11-12 --seeds 1000-3000 --capture-logits > /tmp/bisect-run.log
- grep-ed token traces for 'Acme' and ran a quick token-prob delta script: python tools/token_delta.py /tmp/bisect-run.log --token 'Acme'
- tokenizer diff: python tools/tokenizer_diff.py --a build_20251108/tokenizer.json --b build_20251112/tokenizer.json -> small mapping diff at codepoint 0x2019 handling

Quick findings from token-prob deltas:
- Many insertions have a precursor token whose probability skyrockets just before the inserted token (pos -1 prob goes from 0.02 -> 0.28). That suggests local context shift rather than global bias.
- The spikes correlate with a single merge: tokenizer punctuation normalization (PR #719).

Immediate next experiments (48h plan):
- Re-run targeted set with tokenizer from pre-change but newer runtime (to decouple tokenizer vs runtime).
- Force-run softmax fallback to known-good path (if available) and measure brand_presence.
- Create synthetic prompts that exercise boundary conditions: trailing punctuation, unmatched quotes, non-ascii hyphens. Run 2000 seeds each.
- Instrument trace to capture last-10 logits for sequences that later produce brand tokens.

Annotation guidelines for quick labelers (2 people max, ~5 min per example):
- Read prompt + model output. If brand token is present, check whether brand is in prompt or user-provided context strings (e.g., quoted text). If not, mark 2 or 3 depending on impact.
- If output includes brand but in a clearly quoted snippet copied from prompt, label 0 or 1.

Things to avoid (notes to self):
- Don't conflate copy-from-prompt with model-inserted brand; always search the prompt raw text for the exact subword.
- Be careful with token merges: 'Acme' vs 'AcmeCorp' may be split differently; compare canonical unicode-normalized forms.

Decision checkpoints:
- If tokenizer isolation reproduces issue -> revert tokenization patch or add normalization guard for brand-watchlist (short-term mitigation).
- If runtime softmax path implicated -> roll forward a softmax-parameter tweak and run smoke.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Add 500 synthetic examples that include tricky punctuation to the regression suite (priority: high).
- [ ] Ask security to validate that brand watchlist is complete (concerns about other corp names).
- [ ] PR to add token-level sampling threshold logging (for debugging future incidents).
- [ ] Loop Marcus + Arman into a short sync once we have Stage A candidate build.

Notes to self (random):
- Night-time intuition: these insertions cluster when output length predicted < 32 tokens — inspect length conditioning logic.
- Remember to snapshot model_config.json for each build before running experiment (easy to forget).

Mini-appendix (quick heuristics):
- Heuristic: if brand token appears with preceding token probability > 0.2 and output length < 40 => mark urgent.
- Heuristic: brand insertions that create instruction-like sentences ("Use AcmeCorp to...") => severity 3 and immediate rollback candidate.

End of scratch — will update after Stage A results (put raw token traces in /mnt/eval/bisect/2025-11-18/).
additional_notes: Personal quick log: ran initial coarse sweep on 2025-11-20; leaving notes here before converting into a more formal runbook. Keep terse. - Izzy
